protocol.py: 6 biology problems (3 errors, 3 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: pcr mix (well A1 in slot 2)
   line 28:  p300.aspirate(20, pcr_reservoir["A1"])
   At line 28 the tip went into pcr mix (well A1 in slot 2) while it still carried colony 1
   (well A1 in slot 4), colony 2 (well A2 in slot 4), colony 3 (well A3 in slot 4), colony 4
   (well A4 in slot 4) and 11 more from an earlier step (this line did it 15 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this
   stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the
   unwanted material along into 15 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 7
   more in slot 3.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 15 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 7 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 28 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [5bae3dd5431a]

2. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 16 stocks
   line 32:  p300.aspirate(1, colony_plate[well_name])
   At line 32 the tip went into colony 1 (well A1 in slot 4), colony 2 (well A2 in slot 4),
   colony 3 (well A3 in slot 4), colony 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 12 more while it still
   carried pcr mix (well A1 in slot 2), colony 1 (well A1 in slot 4), colony 2 (well A2 in
   slot 4), colony 3 (well A3 in slot 4) and 12 more from an earlier step (this line did it
   16 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 14 other wells: wells A3, A4, A5, A6, A7,
   A8, A9, A10 and 6 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 8 more in slot 4.
   Also reached 14 other wells: wells A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10 and 6 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 32 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [3e35d99c2ec9]

3. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 1 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 32:  p300.aspirate(1, colony_plate[well_name])
   At line 32 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 1 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 16 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 8 more in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 8 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [64c34912ee27]

4. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 28:  p300.aspirate(20, pcr_reservoir["A1"])
   At line 28 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 2 while it still carried colony
   1 (well A1 in slot 4), colony 2 (well A2 in slot 4), colony 3 (well A3 in slot 4), colony
   4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 11 more from an earlier step (this line did it 15 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the
   protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the
   master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate.
   A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a
   no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected
   wells, and the unwanted material went along into 15 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5,
   A6, A7, A8, A9 and 7 more in slot 3.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 15 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 7 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 28, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [e32dafb2ca4c]

5. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 16 wells of pcr mix with a sample
   line 30:  p300.dispense(20, pcr_plate[well_name])
   At line 30 the robot starts putting pcr mix into Bio-Rad 96 Well Plate 200 µL PCR (slot
   3), and 16 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the
   mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated,
   or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate
   can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 8 more in
   slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 8 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 20 ul of pcr mix and 1 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [d5449c825d2e]

6. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 16 wells never mixed after colony 1, colony 2, colony 3, colony 4
and 12 more went in (5% of the well)
   line 34:  p300.dispense(1, pcr_plate[well_name])
   At line 34 the robot added colony 1, colony 2, colony 3, colony 4 and 12 more to wells
   A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 8 more in slot 3, which already held pcr mix (this
   line did it 16 times). The addition was 5% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 8 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 8 more in slot 3 after line 34:
   `mix_after=(5, 17)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 17, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [997d5953c5fd]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
